analysis.topic: Rising competition from existing home sellers is squeezing builder margins and forcing price cuts.
key_facts: Lennar's west region average price dropped 7% YoY (p3)
21% of existing-home sellers dropped asking prices in the 4 weeks through Sept 20 (p5)
45% of home sellers gave concessions in August (p6)
Lennar's gross margin is 15.8%, matching post-2008 levels (p14)
Cost to buy down rate on $100M forward commitment rose to $5.4M (p17)
New home sales per community fell 18% in September vs August (p18)

quotes.text: Builders will have to cough up money if they want to stay competitive with the swelling inventory on the market.
quotes.speaker: Author
quotes.why: Summarizes the core financial pressure on builders

timeline_events.event: New home sales rose 7% as builders filled inventory gaps.
45% of home sellers offered concessions to buyers.
21% of existing-home sellers dropped asking prices in the prior four weeks.
Berkshire Hathaway paid $6.8 billion to buy Taylor Morrison.
Berkshire Hathaway raised its stake in Lennar above 10%.

visual_assets.value: Photo of construction worker framing a house, directly illustrating the builder subject.
Bar chart showing Lennar's sales incentives as a percentage of revenue, supporting the margin discussion.
